claims.text: The preserved source asks only to hand-write EventEmitter with on, emit, once and off; return values, duplicate-removal semantics, mutation-during-emit behavior and error handling are not source constraints, so the answer labels them explicit candidate-contract choices.
Removing a once record before invoking its listener prevents synchronous reentrant emit from executing that once registration twice under the candidate contract.

The exact candidate fixture verifies registration order, argument forwarding, emitter this binding, stable per-emit snapshots, and that on/off mutations affect later rounds rather than changing the current snapshot.

The candidate explicitly chooses off(event, listener) to remove all registrations sharing the same original function, including once records, and the deterministic fixture verifies that documented choice.

findings: The answer preserves the narrow four-method source and does not claim undocumented Node.js compatibility.
Unspecified semantics that materially affect correctness are explicit contract choices rather than source facts.
Original-listener identity and registration-record identity are separated so off(originalFn) can cancel once while a fired once record is removed precisely.
The once listener is removed before invocation and the reentrancy fixture proves it cannot fire twice through synchronous recursive emit.
A stable snapshot gives deterministic mutation-during-emit behavior and the fixture verifies current-round and next-round observations.
Duplicate-off and exception-propagation choices are explicit and tested.
